content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a medium beef patty, melted cheese, fresh vegetables, sauce, and a bun. It is quick to prepare and popular worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger appeared in the United States in the 1920s.
There are more than 50 topping variations, including bacon, fried onions, and a range of sauces.
In Japan, cheeseburgers are often served with teriyaki sauce and seaweed.
The world’s largest cheeseburger weighed over 300 kg and was made in the US in 2012.
Cheeseburgers are frequently used in advertising as a symbol of quick, affordable food.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and cheese supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of protein, fat, and carbohydrates provides a quick energy boost.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cheeseburgers are calorie‑dense due to fats and carbs, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat and sodium
items.content: High levels of saturated fat and salt can raise cholesterol and blood pressure.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Undercooked or low‑quality meat can harbor bacteria; ensure the patty is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cheeseburgers are typically eaten with the hands, holding the bottom bun. They are often served with fries, a dipping sauce, or a beverage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in plastic. Reheat in an oven or microwave to keep the bun from becoming soggy.
